findings.detail: The question repeats the problem of the earlier questions M2-S40-T1 and M3-S50-T2. All three ask the reader to recognize that direct execution fits simple, well-scoped changes, and the same reasoning leads to the answer. The correct option C reuses the same example as M2-S40-T1: a single validation check in one function. Changing the frame from 'which task' or 'which approach' to 'which rule' does not create a different problem. Wrong option A (microservice restructuring through direct execution) echoes M3-S50-T2. Wrong option B (always plan before every edit) echoes M2-S40-T1.

blind_answer.reason: Direct execution suits simple, well-scoped changes such as adding a single validation check to one function. A is wrong because a microservice restructuring needs plan mode whatever the deadline. B is wrong because it forces planning for every change. D is wrong because many-file changes with open design choices call for plan mode.
